title: Declarative Rules - Quiz
description: Test your understanding of declarative rules concepts in PEGA

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of declarative rules over procedural logic?
options: They automatically recalculate when dependencies change
questions.explanation: Declarative rules automatically recalculate when their dependencies change, eliminating the need for manual updates and ensuring data consistency throughout the application.

questions.question: Which declarative rule type is best for calculating derived values?
questions.explanation: Declare Expression rules are specifically designed for calculating derived values based on other properties, automatically updating when source values change.

questions.question: When should you use a Declare Constraint rule?
options: To enforce business rules and validate data
questions.explanation: Declare Constraint rules enforce business rules and validate data by ensuring properties meet specific conditions, automatically checking when values change.

questions.question: What happens when a Declare Trigger rule fires?
options: It executes an activity when specified conditions are met
questions.explanation: Declare Trigger rules execute activities when specified conditions are met, allowing automatic processing when data changes without explicit user action.

questions.question: How do declarative rules improve maintainability?
options: By centralizing business logic and reducing procedural code
questions.explanation: Declarative rules centralize business logic and reduce procedural code, making applications more maintainable by eliminating scattered validation and calculation logic.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Declare Index rules?
options: To create database indexes for performance
To expose embedded properties for reporting and searching
questions.explanation: Declare Index rules expose embedded properties for reporting and searching by creating virtual properties that can be accessed like top-level properties.

questions.question: When should you avoid using declarative rules?
options: For complex business logic requiring external system calls
questions.explanation: Declarative rules should be avoided for complex business logic requiring external system calls, as they are designed for in-memory processing and may impact performance.

questions.question: How do you optimize declarative rule performance?
options: By carefully designing target properties and avoiding circular dependencies
questions.explanation: Declarative rule performance is optimized by carefully designing target properties, avoiding circular dependencies, and ensuring rules fire only when necessary.
